senses.gloss:
icchāśakti
(‘power of will’)
------------------------------------------
According to the Vedānta philosophy, हिरण्यगर्भ is the second aspect of ब्रह्मन्, the Absolute. He is pure चोन्स्चिओउस्नेस्स् associated with अज्ञान or nescience, and comes after ईश्वर in the process of च्रेअतिओन्. He is endowed with three powers of icchā or will, ज्ञान or knowledge, and kriyā or action. These three powers are respectively known as इच्छाशक्ति, ज्ञानशक्ति, and क्रियाशक्ति. By इच्छाशक्ति he controls the animate and inanimate aspects of च्रेअतिओन्.
According to the शैवसिद्धान्त (Śaivism as developed in Tamil Nadu) these three śaktis evolve out of the union of Paraśiva and पराशक्ति. They are, respectively, pure ज्ञान (knowledge) and pure kriyā (activity).
Icchāśakti is a combination of ज्ञान and kriyā in equal proportion. क्रियाशक्ति is a combination in which kriyā is in excess of ज्ञान. ज्ञानशक्ति is a combination in which ज्ञान is in excess of kriyā.
